decision_log.decision: Organise the room as three parallel strips along the long east-west axis: a 1.00 m entry/service gallery at the west end under a 2.10 m soffit (door and closet press), a central study field at 2.40 m, and a sleeping bay against the east wall.
decision_log.rationale: Keeps the room reading as one long low bar with the service functions gathered in a lower, narrower strip offset to one end instead of scattered round the room.

decision_log.decision: Entry door 0.90 m wide at the south end of the west short wall (offset 0.20), a flush oak leaf in a concealed frame with no architrave, hinged on the south jamb and opening inward into the gallery.
decision_log.rationale: A plain flush door at a wall end arriving in a compressed vestibule beside the solid closet mass, from which the room opens eastward; door, window band and desk share no centreline.

decision_log.decision: One 3.30 m window band on the south long wall (x 0.30-3.60, 78.6% of the wall): three 0.84 m glazed bays, each a pair of 0.42 m outward-opening casements, alternating with two 0.39 m framed stippled infill panels on a 1.23 m module; sill course top at 0.74, head at 2.10 under the soffit.
decision_log.rationale: A continuous ribbon of tall narrow lights on the ~1.22 m module with a continuous sill course and head at the ceiling band, never a single picture window; the framed solid panels take the place of piers so the band is one buildable opening and its span is unambiguous against the brief.

decision_log.decision: Casements glazed with straight-line leaded ladder bars and a chevron head; the infill panels are stippled plaster in oak frames matching the lights.
decision_log.rationale: Where glass is detailed it is a straight-line leaded lattice; solid panels interrupting a band are framed like the lights they replace.

decision_log.decision: Band end piers unequal, 0.30 m brick at the west and 0.60 m at the east, so the band stops short of both corners without making the south wall bilaterally symmetrical; the wider east pier backs the bed.
decision_log.rationale: The composition must be asymmetric overall while each light stays symmetric within itself.

decision_log.decision: Built-in desk (1.60 x 0.60) and built-in shelving (2.00 x 0.35) on the north wall as one run from x 0.60 to 4.20: a continuous oak datum slab at 0.70-0.74 is both desk top and sill-height shelf; shelf slabs at 1.46 and 1.82 run uninterrupted over desk and shelving; a pale cast-stone cap at 2.04-2.10 sits under the head band; uprights are set back and unemphasised.
decision_log.rationale: Shelf and plinth slabs run uninterrupted round the room and no vertical element is emphasised; joinery is stacked slabs and square posts with an oversailing top and a thinner rail beneath, and the top of the built-in gets a plain light-toned cap.

decision_log.decision: Storage without freestanding wardrobes: a built-in closet press 0.60 x 2.40 x 2.10 on the west wall, a cupboard bank under the shelving, a three-drawer desk pedestal, two drawers under the bed platform and an open bedside ledge.
decision_log.rationale: Storage and coats belong in the service strip beside the entry; all pulls are square on a grid with no applied ornament.

decision_log.decision: Built-in oak platform bed 0.90 x 2.00 against the east wall (x 3.30-4.20, y 0.60-2.60), head to the north, mattress top at 0.45, no headboard, drawers below; a built-in bedside ledge 0.90 x 0.45 x 0.60 fills the gap to the shelving.
decision_log.rationale: A low stacked-slab platform keeps the long low reading and uses the plain brick wall and its stone band as the backdrop instead of a headboard.

decision_log.decision: Flat ceiling field at 2.40 m with a 0.30 m deep perimeter dropped soffit at 2.10 m that oversails the window heads and reads as a continuous head band at door-head height; the soffit widens to 1.00 m over the entry gallery.
decision_log.rationale: The ceiling edge is a deep horizontal band oversailing the glazing like an eave; ceilings are flat; the entry arrives under a compressed ceiling.

decision_log.decision: Materials: exposed tawny brick with raked horizontal joints and flush vertical joints on the east wall, the window-wall piers and the back wall of the desk/shelving run; every masonry or joinery edge capped with a plain pale cast-stone band (sill course, plinth, cap slabs); oak joinery of stacked rectangular slabs and square posts; no curved mouldings, no mirror panels, no gloss lacquer.
decision_log.rationale: Brick is exposed only as horizontal coursing and every edge gets a light-toned cap; profiles are stepped rectangular layers with no carving or turning.

decision_log.decision: Warm palette: tawny brick and oiled oak dominant with pale stone bands, fumed oak floor and warm stippled plaster; copper and oxblood leather as accents.
decision_log.rationale: Dark brick bands between light horizontal strips, oak woodwork and copper and leather accents, kept warm throughout.

decision_log.decision: Floor: fumed oak boards laid east-west in the main room, red quarry tile in the 1.00 m entry gallery strip.
decision_log.rationale: Boards along the long axis reinforce the horizontal reading; the hard tile marks the service strip at the entry.

decision_log.decision: Proportions set by four horizontal datums that run round the room: plinth 0.10, sill/desk 0.74, shelf 1.50, head band 2.10; bays and slabs are much wider than tall, lights much taller than wide (0.42 x 1.36).
decision_log.rationale: Continuous sill course and head band at door-head height keep the room long and low; main-storey lights are tall and narrow on a regular module.

decision_log.decision: Lighting: a concealed continuous LED cove on the inner edge of the perimeter soffit washing the ceiling field, a linear task light in a copper channel under the 1.46 shelf slab, a recessed slot in the gallery soffit and one small square bedside fitting; no pendants or vertical fittings.
decision_log.rationale: Light is laid in as horizontal lines within the band and slabs so nothing vertical is emphasised and the eave-like band reads as the source.

decision_log.decision: A copper-lined planter trough is built onto the window sill course for the full 3.30 m band.
decision_log.rationale: Planting is built in as a low trough on the sill rather than freestanding pots.

decision_log.decision: Freestanding oak desk chair with square posts, stepped cap finials, three-layer crest cap, stepped block feet and an oxblood leather seat; tall narrow back 1.02 x 0.45.
decision_log.rationale: Chair built from square posts and stacked layers with no carving or turning.

decision_log.decision: No fireplace or chimney breast: the brief asks for none and the room has no internal core wall, so the hearth and chimney rules are not applied.
decision_log.rationale: A rule is cited only where it genuinely supports a decision.

conflicts.constraint: Brief: one window band, a bed, built-in storage and a desk/shelving wall in a 4.20 x 3.60 m room
conflicts.resolution: No end wall is free for a full-width window group between piers: the east wall takes the bed and the west wall the door and closet press. The single window band goes on the long south wall per R07/R11. Brief favoured on buildability.

conflicts.constraint: Brief: window band must span at least 50% of one wall's length (measured from spec.json openings)
conflicts.resolution: The band is one 3.30 m structural opening (78.6%) rather than three casement openings between brick piers; the 1.23 m pier rhythm is kept with 0.39 m framed solid infill panels (R15) in place of brick piers. Brief favoured on the measured span; rule kept on rhythm and proportion.

The structural ceiling stays at 2.40 m throughout; the compressed vestibule is an applied 0.30 m dropped soffit (2.10 m) confined to the entry gallery and the perimeter band, and the main field keeps the brief height.

conflicts.constraint: Brief: study/bedroom with a bed and 0.90 m circulation; no terrace or balcony stated
conflicts.resolution: Floor-to-head glazed leaves opening onto a terrace do not apply; the band is taken as tall outward-opening casements over a 0.74 m sill course (R07) that also carries the built-in planter trough (R10).
